protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 2 of 3; refute not confirm; verify C2-D044-01 and NOTE-C2-D044-01 landed
summary: C2-D044-01 landed exactly as scoped and not as the silent file-09 conversion the dispatch warns against: the claim-matrix Key sealed laws pin is now named with its path, identified as the sixth whole-document freeze pin in file 08's D-014 accounting note, excluded on both grounds, routed to a later file-09 D-000 act, and left whole-document -- with a matching rejected alternative. I confirmed file 09 is untouched and its pin is still whole-document, which is what 'left whole-document' has to mean at the bytes. NOTE-C2-D044-01 landed too: clause 2 now says both occurrences of the baseline-refresh sentence cease to be live scope. I re-derived all fifteen segment hashes and the §7.10 example rather than relying on the byte-identity claim, and I verified that claim independently by hashing the four spans the prompt says are unchanged. One thing was removed silently: the re-measurement clause in the Measured-inputs header. I nearly graded that a SHOULD-FIX and did not, because measurement showed it is a drafting convention that appears zero times in adopted COORD entries, its function was discharged by this review, and nothing drifted.

notesRecorded.observation: The re-measurement clause was dropped during the repair and its removal is not disclosed. Turn 1 read 'Measured inputs (re-measure at dispatch if any cited file moved):'. Turn 2 reads 'Measured inputs:'. A token-loss diff over the whole draft returns exactly four lost tokens -- dispatch, if, moved, re-measure -- all from that line, and I confirmed no re-measure, remeasure, 'if a cited file', or 'moves' language survives anywhere else in the draft.
notesRecorded.whyIAlmostGradedItHigher: This is the most digest-dense entry in the series -- fifteen segment hashes, five whole-file digests and two commit references -- its entire subject is pin fidelity, and the clause is the mechanism that protects those pins against drift between drafting and adoption. That drift is not hypothetical here: COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md moved between the D-043 and D-044 dispatches, and the freeze itself moved at D-014. Silent removal during an otherwise additive repair is also the exact failure mode that caught the DR-005 v2 repair and that I flagged when D-042 turn 2 dropped MF-6.
notesRecorded.whyItIsOnlyANote: I measured rather than assumed, and the measurement cut against the higher grade. 'If a cited file moves, re-measure' occurs ZERO times in adopted COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md entries; re-measure language of any kind occurs twice in the whole file. The clause is a drafting-stage instruction to the dispatch and the reviewers, not part of what a recording carries into the register, so dropping it has no effect on the adopted record. Its function was in fact discharged: I re-measured every cited digest this turn and all twenty reproduce. And the environment did not move between turns -- HEAD a5d3719, COORD 726b472e, file 08 877e36d3, freeze e809d439, blueprint 909394c5 and the claim matrix b96f6236 are identical to my turn-1 measurements. Blocking consent over a transient drafting aid whose job I performed anyway would be inflating a finding.
notesRecorded.residualWorthCarrying: Turn 3 and adoption are still ahead, and this series has seen the environment move between dispatches more than once. If any cited file moves before adoption, nothing in these bytes instructs anyone to re-measure. Restoring the parenthetical costs one line.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: ac109dbca4da41441aef8e5302e9070f12914115ccfc3760751fbd669625ff6d both times, matching the dispatch's expected digest. No drift.

C2-D044-01 landed in the form I asked for and not as a conversion. My remedy asked that the claim-matrix pin be named, scoped out, and routed rather than folded in. The new paragraph does all four: it names the pin with its path 'docs/v2/architecture/09-v1-to-v2-claim-matrix.md', identifies it as 'the sixth whole-document freeze pin in file 08's D-014 pin-accounting note', excludes it on both grounds -- 'outside this entry's file-08 scope and outside D-033 clause 1's DR-row list' -- states 'This entry does not convert it', and routes it: 'routed to a later file-09 D-000 act and stays whole-document until then.' A matching rejected alternative was added: 'Also convert the claim-matrix Key sealed laws pin in this commit. Rejected: file 09 is a separate register-content act.'

The attack 'landed as a silent conversion of file 09' fails at the bytes, which is the only place it could be tested. docs/v2/architecture/09-v1-to-v2-claim-matrix.md is unmodified in git, measures b96f623690ea28fa2c3a… unchanged from turn 1, and still carries exactly one whole-document freeze digest occurrence. 'Stays whole-document until then' is true of the file, not just of the sentence.

The accounting claim is exact. File 08's D-014 note reads 'six freeze pins — five in this register (DR-004, DR-005, DR-006, DR-011, DR-012) plus one in the claim matrix (**Key sealed laws**)', which is precisely what the new paragraph asserts. I matched it over normalized whitespace because the note spans blockquote-continued lines.

NOTE-C2-D044-01 landed. Clause 2 now closes with 'Both occurrences of "A baseline refresh re-opens it" in the DR-001 cell cease to be live scope.' That converts my measurement into an instruction the performing commit can be checked against, which is what the note was for. The disposition table records it accurately, including that clause 2 already retired the sentence and that the performing commit must retire both occurrences.

The attack 'pin table or extraction hashes changed' fails, verified two independent ways rather than one. First by content: I re-derived all fifteen segment hashes from the live freeze and blueprint this turn and every one reproduces, plus the §7.10 worked example at 7bfa72c4…. Second by structure: I hashed the pin-table span in both drafts and it is byte-identical at e3b0549d…, and the extraction-rule section is byte-identical at ccfcfae2… even though the prompt did not claim that section was unchanged.

I did not accept the prompt's byte-identity assertion for the decision clauses either. I extracted and hashed clause 1 (c7a5734e…) and clauses 3 through 7 (63a2c6ca…) from both drafts independently; both spans match. The claim holds.

The token-loss diff over the entire draft returns exactly four tokens, all from the Measured-inputs header, and I traced the only other two lines diff reports as removed -- 'history.' and 'here.' -- to line rewraps where clause 2 and the DR-001 paragraph were expanded, confirmed against the corresponding added lines. Nothing else was lost anywhere.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on all six recitals: file 08 877e36d3…, freeze e809d439…, blueprint 909394c5…, COORD 726b472e…, Claude 2 turn 1 0e6ee95d…, Codex turn 1 db0452a3…. Each measured by me against live bytes.

My turn-1 verdict is characterized exactly: 'OBJECT, 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX'. That is what I returned, my single objection id C2-D044-01 appears in the disposition table as ACCEPTED, and my note appears separately as RECORDED, so neither was dropped or merged away.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED or SATISFIED re-record' fails. All occurrences are negative or historical and sit inside clauses 3 through 7, which I verified byte-identical to turn 1: 'The 2026-08-13 SATISFIED disposition stays history', 'This entry is not that re-record', 'No row becomes SATISFIED', 'Zero SATISFIED', and the rejected alternative. Preserving the 2026-08-13 disposition as history rather than deleting it remains the correct handling.

The attacks 'MEASURED regeneration bundled', 'DESIGN-READY / new status token', 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'freeze / blueprint motion' all fail, and all sit in the byte-identical span. Clause 4 defers regeneration and states this entry is not it; clause 5 keeps the status vocabulary closed citing D-006 turn-2 NOTE-03; clause 6 states condition 5 unchanged, no freeze motion, no blueprint, no docs/v2/implementation/; DESIGN-READY is rejected in the alternatives citing D-033 clause 4.

D-033 remains characterized correctly as authorizing and expressly not performing, in both the decision-type line and the measured-inputs row, matching adopted D-033 clause 2's own words. The adoption commits ac48808 for D-033 and a5d3719 for D-043 are both correct.

File 08, the freeze, the blueprint, COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md and the claim matrix are all unmodified in git. Nothing has been pre-applied ahead of this entry's own adoption, consistent with the rewrite being performed only by the commit this entry authorizes.

Examined and declined again, carried forward from turn 1: clause 3 still restates D-033's SATISFIED gate as 'SATISFIED only after independent review' where D-033 says 'after DR-204 audits the disposition', and DR-204 is still named zero times. This sits inside the byte-identical clauses 3-7 span, so it is unchanged rather than newly introduced. I decline it for the same reason as at turn 1 -- the constraint survives and clause 3 points at D-001 as governing -- and I record it again so that declining it twice is a visible choice rather than an omission.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex turn-2 review of D-044. Not read. It exists at review time and I hashed it without opening: 2f4255025b1ec2105a691deed61a510b362c555510a999ce79959983701afab3.

The Codex turn-1 verdict, hashed but never opened. The entry characterizes it as CONSENT with 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX and lists NOTE-D044-01 as an adoption instruction that is 'not a merits condition'. I verified the digest db0452a3… only. If that characterization is wrong -- if Codex in fact raised something -- the turn-2 premise that only my findings needed disposition fails, and nothing in my review would detect it.

The substantive content of the fifteen pinned sections. I verified boundaries, hashes, and that each is cited by its row; not that the pinned text discharges what the row needs from it. That is the row owners' question and it is the limit I have carried on every property-pin review in this series.

Whether the claim-matrix pin should itself become a property pin, and what §6's segment hash would be. I verified only that it exists, is still whole-document, is accurately described, and is now routed.

Whether any whole-document pin exists in a file neither I nor the register's accounting note has swept. I checked file 08 and the claim matrix, the two the D-014 note identifies; I did not sweep every document in the repository.

Whether the performing commit will in fact retire both occurrences of the baseline-refresh sentence. That is what NOTE-C2-D044-01 and clause 2's new sentence exist to make checkable at that commit, not here.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX, and I state what I attacked so the consent is not read as a light pass. My turn-1 objection was a silence about the sixth tracked freeze pin; it is now named, doubly scoped out, routed to a later file-09 act, and backed by a rejected alternative -- and I checked the bytes rather than the sentence, confirming file 09 is untouched and its pin still whole-document. I re-derived all fifteen segment hashes instead of trusting that an unchanged table stays correct, and I hashed the four spans the prompt calls byte-identical instead of accepting the assertion. The one silent removal I found, the re-measurement clause, I nearly graded a SHOULD-FIX; I measured instead and found it appears zero times in adopted entries, so it is a drafting aid rather than record content, its function was discharged by this review, and nothing drifted. It is a note, with the residual named for turn 3.
